summary.title: Best friend did not mark my birthday
summary.what_happened: My best friend of ten years did not contact me on my birthday. There was no message or call, while people I barely know did text me. For the last two or three weeks she had been quiet and slow to reply. I assumed she was busy with work. Last year I organised a surprise dinner for her birthday. I have not told her how I feel. Since my birthday I have been ignoring her messages.
summary.my_feelings: I feel hurt that she forgot, especially after ten years of friendship and after what I did for her birthday last year.
summary.my_needs: I need to feel that I matter to her and that our friendship is mutual.
summary.desired_outcome: I want her to realise how much it hurt.

consult.text:
It makes sense that this hurt. A ten-year friend saying nothing on your birthday, while people you barely know remembered, would sting most people. It is even harder after the effort you put into her birthday last year.

Here is one way she may see it. You said she has been quiet and slow to reply for weeks. That could mean she is dealing with something, like work pressure or something personal, and her birthday message slipped past her. Forgetting is not the same as not caring, though I can't know which it is.

One thing that may have made this harder is that she does not know she hurt you. Since your birthday you have been ignoring her messages. From her side, that may look like you pulling away for no reason, and she may be wondering what she did.

The main unknowns are why she was quiet and whether she knows she missed the day.

Some next steps:
1. Reply to her, even briefly, so the silence stops adding to the confusion.
2. Tell her plainly what happened on your birthday and how it felt.
3. Ask how she has been these past few weeks.
Why are you making excuses for her? She forgot. Period.

I am not excusing her. She missed something that mattered to you, and your hurt is real. You are allowed to expect more from a close friend.

I also can't tell you she did it on purpose, because I only have your side and I don't know what was going on for her. Both things can be true. She let you down, and there may be a reason that has nothing to do with how she feels about you.

What I would hold on to is this. If you want her to understand how much it hurt, she needs to hear it from you. Right now she can't know. Ignoring her messages may feel like a fair response, but it makes it less likely she will ever see the hurt, because she may only see you going quiet.

You don't have to let it go or pretend it was fine. You can be direct and still be honest about being hurt. Try something like: "I was really hurt that you didn't say anything on my birthday." Then see how she responds. That will tell you much more than the silence can.

I also haven't been replying to your messages since then, and that wasn't fair to you, because I hadn't told you why. I noticed you've seemed quiet lately, and I don't know what has been going on for you. I would like to understand. Could we talk, on the phone or in person, when it suits you? I'd really like to hear how you've been and how you see this.
